issues.issue: The provision is paragraph 11 but disqualifies any payment not made "strictly pursuant to the requirements of this paragraph 10 and Attachment A," a mis-numbered self-reference pointing instead to the Application of Payments clause. The mechanical error leaves it uncertain which requirements a payment must satisfy to count as received.

"[F]or the duration of this Agreement and thereafter" sets no end point for the reporting of the pre-Agreement delinquent payment status. How long "thereafter" runs, and on what status, is not ascertainable from the words used.

Default is triggered by failure to pay "all other amounts Customer agreed to pay" and "other amounts that may attain priority over the Security Instrument," categories with no stated boundary appended to the specific items (taxes, insurance, senior liens). What non-payment forfeits the workout is therefore indeterminate.

The integration clause declaring this Agreement to supersede all prior understandings conflicts with the accompanying Aurora cover letter, which states that "[s]igning the attached documents in no way affects or eliminates any rights you have been given in this letter" and adds bankruptcy terms "[n]ot withstanding anything to the contrary contained in the Special Forbearance Agreement." Whether the letter survives integration is squarely contestable.

Paragraph 15 requires receipt of payments on or before "the Due Dates specified in Attachment A," but Attachment A defines "Due Date" as the 15th of each month while fixing the First Plan payment for 11/18/2009. The time-of-the-essence rule therefore has no clear date to attach to the first payment.

The Agreement is said to "inure to the benefit of" any subsequent servicer or holder without stating that a transferee assumes Lender's forbearance obligations under paragraph 3. Whether a successor servicer is bound as well as benefited is left unaddressed.

The proviso that "no such severability shall be effective if it materially changes the economic benefit of this Agreement to either party" turns on "materially changes the economic benefit," a standard the Agreement nowhere defines or measures. It also leaves unsaid what happens to the Agreement if severance is thereby made ineffective.

"[T]he address above" is ambiguous where the instrument prints several different Aurora addresses (Scottsbluff Loss Mitigation, the Littleton and Denver Cashiering addresses). Which address a Customer notice or inquiry should go to is not fixed.

The First Plan payment is due "on or before 11/18/2009," but the effectiveness condition in Attachment A requires Lender to receive that payment by the Agreement Return Date of 11/15/2009, and the cover letter demands it by 11/15/2009. A payment made on the date this provision allows would fail the condition another provision imposes.

The 11/15/2009 Agreement Return Date cannot be squared with the preceding sentence of the same paragraph, which allows the First Plan payment "on or before 11/18/2009," once the effectiveness clause ties both to the Return Date. Which of the two dates governs the initial payment is left unresolved.

The condition that the Agreement be "of no force and effect" absent receipt of the executed Agreement and First Plan payment by the Agreement Return Date conflicts with a.1's grant of until 11/18/2009 for that payment. Whether the Agreement ever took effect thus turns on which date controls.

The First Plan payment must be in "certified funds" but the permitted means include a money order and a Western Union transfer, instruments not obviously certified funds. What tender satisfies the condition of effectiveness is therefore uncertain.

"[S]hall be payable in certified funds as described above are to be sent to Lender's Payment Processing Center" is missing a conjunction, running two obligations together as one ungrammatical sentence. The defect obscures whether the mailing instruction is itself a condition of a conforming payment under paragraph 11.

"Plan payments are to be paid on or before the 15th day of every month" states no end date, while a.1 fixes exactly six payments running through 04/15/2010. Whether monthly payments continue past the Sixth Plan payment is left open between the two paragraphs.

The Expiration Date is the Due Date of the Sixth Plan payment, yet Attachment A paragraph b imposes the duty to cure the Arrearage "[u]pon the Expiration Date," and paragraph 2 says the Agreement then expires. Whether the Agreement can impose a cure obligation on or after the day it terminates is unresolved.

The clause presupposes a pending "request for a loan modification or other workout option" but nowhere states any Lender duty to consider, evaluate or decide that request, nor any deadline or standard for doing so. Whether providing the financial information earns the borrower an evaluation, or merely a gratuitous opportunity, is exactly what the words leave open.

The obligation to submit modification support after the Second Plan payment sits against Attachment A's statement that tender of the Sixth Plan payment "shall not be deemed acceptance ... of a workout plan or loan modification" and paragraph b's "Cure Method" that Lender "may offer." Read together, it is unclear whether the modification process is a contractual undertaking at all.

The documents are required "to enable Lender to properly evaluate" the modification request, language that implies an evaluation without imposing one, and the provision sets no deadline for submission or for Lender's response. Whether "properly evaluate" is a promise the borrower can enforce is left ambiguous.

The disclaimer that tender of the Sixth Plan payment is not acceptance of "a workout plan or loan modification" cannot easily be squared with a.2's requirement that the Customer submit financial information in support of a modification request and with paragraph b's requirement to enter a Cure Method upon expiration. What performance of the plan actually purchases is left contradictory.

The statement that the aggregate Plan payments will be insufficient and the account will remain delinquent conflicts with the recital that Lender agreed to allow Customer "to repay the Arrearage pursuant to a loan work-out arrangement" and with paragraph 4's reference to full reinstatement. A court would have to decide what the plan was for if it could never cure the default.

The Customer "must cure the Arrearage" through a Cure Method that includes "other loan workout option that Lender may offer," making the borrower's compliance depend on an option Lender has discretion whether to extend. "Cure Method" thus states a mandatory duty whose means may never come into existence.

Failure to enter a Cure Method triggers foreclosure "as specified in paragraphs 6 and 8," yet that failure occurs upon the Expiration Date, when paragraph 2 says the Agreement has expired and paragraph 6's "Default" machinery no longer operates. Which mechanism authorizes the foreclosure at that point is unresolved.
